claims.explanation: TPA is a potent PKC activator that kills cells by forcing sustained PKC-MAPK/ERK signaling, and selectivity likely reflects which tumors retain an intact, PKC-responsive ERK cascade and are not already driven by downstream BRAF/NRAS mutations that uncouple or desensitize this pathway. Lines with BRAF or NRAS mutations (melanomas, some colorectal and thyroid lines) are frequently among the least affected, whereas sensitive lines often have upstream RTK/RAS pathway alterations (EGFR, MAP2K1, KRAS, NF1, MET) or loss of tumor suppressors that leave them dependent on PKC-driven ERK signaling. TP53 mutation is common across both groups and is not by itself selective.

features.basis: BRAF-mutant melanoma/colorectal lines are enriched among least-affected lines, consistent with downstream ERK activation bypassing PKC dependence
NRAS-mutant melanoma and bladder lines appear among least-affected lines, suggesting constitutive ERK signaling reduces PKC-driven killing
EGFR-mutant lung/esophageal lines are enriched among sensitive lines, consistent with RTK-driven ERK dependence
MAP2K1-mutant NCIH1437 is strongly killed, consistent with MEK/ERK pathway addiction
KRAS-mutant pancreatic, ovarian, and neuroblastoma lines are among sensitive lines, suggesting RAS-MAPK dependence
NF1 loss occurs in several sensitive lines (thyroid, upper aerodigestive, sarcoma), consistent with RAS pathway activation
MET-mutant HGC27 is strongly killed, consistent with RTK-driven ERK signaling
TPA induces PTGS2 (TIS10) as a primary response gene, and high baseline expression may mark PKC-responsive tumors
PKC activation by TPA triggers ErbB-4 ectodomain cleavage and nuclear signaling, so ERBB4-expressing lines may be more responsive
TP53 mutation is common in both sensitive and resistant lines, so it is weak but may blunt apoptotic response
CDKN2A loss appears in several least-affected lines, possibly reflecting reduced senescence/apoptosis coupling
PIK3CA mutation appears in several sensitive lines (ovary, gastric, colorectal), suggesting PI3K pathway crosstalk with PKC
